newsitem.title: USA: National TechTeam stock plunges 37 percent.
newsitem.headline: National TechTeam stock plunges 37 percent.

text.p: The stock of National TechTeam Inc., which supplies call centre support to computer firms, plunged 37 percent Monday after the company warned its second-quarter earnings would fall short of analysts' expectations.
National TechTeam's stock fell $5.88 to $10 a share on Nasdaq, where it was one of the most active issues, with nearly 5.3 million shares traded.

Company Chairman William Coyro said Monday second-quarter performance would only break even, hurt by project delays in the first half of 1997 for the company's call centre services and significant start-up costs from a number of new contracts.

The most recent analysts' consensus for National TechTeam's second quarter was 14 cents a share, according to First Call, compared with 9 cents a share a year ago. The company is due to report second-quarter results Aug. 1.

National TechTeam's stock began tumbling a week ago as investor jitters about the Dearborn, Mich.-based company's second-quarter results set in. The stock fell $4 before the announcement Monday, having slid $6 last week.

National TechTeam has been a high-flying stock, rising to $30 a share last year from $3.50 in 1995. The company has also been praised by Michigan Gov. John Engler as one of the state's fastest growing companies.

In his statement, Coyro said the company expects to announce a number of new contracts in the second half of the year. National TechTeam has allocated a large amount of infrastructure, development, sales, and marketing costs related to the contracts to the second quarter, he said.

"TechTeam is in a very strong position with regard both to the quantity and quality of new business that it has today," he said. "Demand for TechTeam's services continues to be strong, and we believe the call centre and corporate computer service industries will continue to grow worldwide."
The company provides clients with telephone support for computer products and end-users, as well as corporate computer services, including technical staffing, systems integration and training.
